matchingWeights.title: Matching Algorithm Weights
matchingWeights.subtitle: Customize how the matching algorithm scores candidates by adjusting the relative importance of each matching method.

technical.name: Technical
technical.description: Keyword-heavy matching for technical roles requiring exact skill matching (e.g., developers, engineers)

creative.name: Creative
creative.description: Vector-heavy matching for creative roles requiring conceptual understanding (e.g., designers, copywriters)

executive.name: Executive
executive.description: Balanced matching for executive roles requiring comprehensive evaluation

balanced.name: Balanced
balanced.description: Even distribution across all matching methods for generalist roles

keyword.label: Keyword Matching
keyword.description: Direct skill matching including synonyms, fuzzy matching, and compound skills
keyword.explanation: Performs direct matching of skills with support for synonyms (e.g., PostgreSQL ≈ SQL), fuzzy matching for typos, and compound skills (e.g., C/C++). Best for technical roles where exact skills matter.
keyword.examples: Use for: Software developers, engineers, data scientists, DevOps

tfidf.label: TF-IDF Matching
tfidf.description: Weighted scoring based on keyword importance in the job description
tfidf.explanation: Uses TF-IDF to calculate the importance of keywords in the job posting. Important keywords count more toward the score. Helps identify critical requirements.
tfidf.examples: Use for: Role-specific requirements, niche technologies, senior positions

vector.label: Vector Similarity
vector.description: Semantic similarity using AI embeddings for contextual understanding
vector.explanation: Uses sentence-transformers to calculate semantic similarity between resume and job posting. Captures conceptual understanding and transferability of skills.
vector.examples: Use for: Creative roles, leadership positions, career changers, conceptual roles
